item: A stall record lists a statement longer than the request that ended inside it, as evidence only (R206)
summary: The slow-statement rule keeps a row only if it ended inside the request and was not longer than it, which is right for the share (a 56.9 s SAVEPOINT read as 1.023 of a 55.6 s request) but drops the one shape a lock holder has: begun before the request, ended inside it. Reproduced through the real slowquery listeners and note_stall on a SQLite busy-wait (holder 6,001 ms, request 4,541 ms): the record named the waiter's own INSERT (share 0.999) and the holder was absent with no trace (/mnt/project-files/audit-0.5.0/inputs/stall-forensics-item-g.md). The statement evidence now carries began_before (the longest two such rows, each duration_ms, sql to 80 characters, began_before_s, overlap_share clamped to 1) beside the unchanged keys, absent when empty so a record without one costs nothing (125 B with one entry); found, share_of_request and classify are untouched, and the report's method text says the log has no thread id so a holder and a bystander look the same. The 174 s case stays empty. A record that carries one is larger, so the fixed contention line shows fewer records and says so in selection.shown / of.
